name: @forguncy-react-workspace/cell-compiler
//dependencies: `rolldown` is the bundler #6 mandates for the compiler's resolution and code
generation half, pinned to the version this toolchain actually installs
(`vite-plus@0.3.2`). It is a runtime dependency because `src/rolldown-bundler.ts`
implements `CellBundlerPort` with it — the port is the package's own code, not a
test fixture — while `compileCell` itself stays bundler-agnostic behind the port.
Two test-only facts ride on the same pin. #12's generated module is only correct
with respect to the CommonJS-to-ESM interop this bundler applies to it, and that
interop is not visible in the module's own source: the shapes that work and the
shapes that fail silently differ only once a consumer's namespace import enumerates
the module, so the regression builds through the real bundler rather than through a
hand-written copy of its runtime helper. The end-to-end tests likewise run authored
entries through the full `compileCell` path against this exact build.
//devDependencies: Test-only, and pinned to versions measured in this repository rather than to
`react` / `react-dom` are the host versions #5 measured on Forguncy 12.0.100
(React 19.2.7). The host-bridge regression evaluates the generated JSX runtime
adapter against the same React the host injects, so the adapter's key/children
semantics are asserted against real React rather than a stub. Nothing in `src/`
may import React: mapping `react` to the host global is the entire point of #9.
`@forguncy-react-workspace/dependency-resolver` is what the #13 PoC test reads
`compilationDependencies` (with the conformance audit) turn the example's
`fgc.lock.json` into the `dependencies` `compileCell` receives, so the test
exercises the recorded chain rather than a hand-written decision constant.
Test-only: nothing in `src/` imports it, so there is no cycle with the resolver.
